findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 while keeping the earlier 4-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145, and in Ruby the later definition wins, so the preserved 4-arg compatibility definition is dead code. Any existing caller still using the old `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` form binds to the new 3-arg signature: max_width lands in `dimensions`, the max_height Integer lands in `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` in optimize raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer`, crashing that code path at runtime. The deliberate-looking backward-compat shim the diff preserves is silently overridden.

[BUG] The animated-GIF branch (`method_name += "_animated" if !!opts[:allow_animation] && from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) can never trigger from the new call site, because `from` is `tempfile.path` and tempfiles in this flow have no extension: FileHelper.download names the tempfile "discourse-upload-#{type}" (visible at uploads_controller.rb:55) and Rack multipart tempfiles are named with random hex, so the path never ends in `.GIF`. With SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, an animated GIF over max_image_size_kb is downsized using the non-animated `downsize_instructions` (no -coalesce), which mangles or flattens the animation — the user's uploaded GIF loses/breaks animation, defeating the `allow_animation:` option this diff explicitly passes at uploads_controller.rb:67.

[BUG] The server-side download cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, decoupling the API/URL upload size limit from the site setting that previously enforced it. For API callers posting a URL, non-image files up to 10MB are downloaded and stored regardless of the configured max_image_size_kb (the image-only downsize guard at lines 63-71 never runs for them), so an admin who set max_image_size_kb to 4MB silently accepts 10MB non-image uploads via the API URL path; conversely no setting above 10MB can be honored for URL downloads.

[BUG] The downsizing loop exits after 5 attempts even when `tempfile.size` still exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, and the false return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (convert_with returns false when convert exits nonzero) is never checked. If the image cannot be reduced below the limit in 5 passes (e.g., a photograph-heavy PNG where -resize 80% barely reduces bytes) or ImageMagick fails on every iteration, execution falls through to `Upload.create_for` and the oversized file is stored anyway — the upload path silently accepts files exceeding the site's configured maximum instead of rejecting them or raising.

[BUG] The client-side size pre-check is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so the browser rejects any file over 10MB before it ever reaches the server-side downsizing this PR adds. Images larger than 10MB are blocked client-side even though the new server path at uploads_controller.rb:63-71 exists precisely to accept and shrink them; and on sites where the admin raised max_image_size_kb above 10240, previously-permitted uploads between 10MB and the configured limit now regress to a 'file too large' alert.

[ADVISORY] The 413 handler hardcodes `10 * 1024` as the reported limit, but a 413 is produced by the web server's client_max_body_size, which is an independent nginx config value unrelated to this constant. Users who hit a real server 413 are told the maximum is 10240KB even when the actual server limit is different (e.g., nginx set to 5MB or 20MB), so the error message actively misleads them about how much to shrink their upload; any admin tuning client_max_body_size gets a wrong message with no code path to correct it.

[BUG] The client-side upload size check replaces the per-type site setting lookup `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, so admin-configured limits (max_image_size_kb AND max_attachment_size_kb, for every upload type) are silently no longer enforced in the composer. A site with max_attachment_size_kb set below 10MB now lets oversized attachments pass the client check and reach the server, where the user gets a raw server/nginx error instead of the friendly localized 'file_too_large' message the old check produced; admins who change the size settings in the admin panel see no change in client behavior. Also, the new downsize feature is silently capped at 10MB client-side: images between 10MB and whatever the admin intended are rejected with 'file too large' even though the server path in uploads_controller would have downsized them.

[BUG] The 413 handler replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, so the error dialog reports '10 MB' as the limit regardless of what is actually configured. On any site where the web server's client_max_body_size or the site setting differs from 10MB, the user is shown a wrong maximum size in the error message after a 413, and cannot tell what limit they actually exceeded.

[BUG] The API URL-download path replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, dropping admin control over the download cap for API-driven URL fetches of both images and other upload types. An admin who lowers max_image_size_kb to constrain server-side fetching finds API URL uploads still pulling up to 10MB; for non-image URL fetches that were previously bounded by the setting, nothing in this diff re-bounds them below 10MB and no downsizing runs (FileHelper.is_image? gate), so oversized non-image downloads are accepted.

[BUG] The downsizing loop passes `tempfile.path` as the `from` argument, and Rack multipart tempfiles have no file extension, so the `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` check in OptimizedImage.optimize (app/models/optimized_image.rb, the `method_name += "_animated"` branch) never matches; animated GIFs are always downsized with the static `downsize_instructions` even when `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is true. Users uploading animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb get a downsized image whose animation is mangled or reduced by plain ImageMagick resize without the animated-specific instructions — the exact case the allow_animated_thumbnails flag and the `_animated` instruction variant exist to handle; the flag the controller passes is effectively dead on this path.

[BUG] The loop ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (which returns false when the ImageMagick invocation fails via convert_with's exitstatus check), so on conversion failure it re-runs convert against the unchanged file for the remaining attempts and then falls through to `Upload.create_for` with a still-oversize or damaged file. A single ImageMagick failure (missing delegate, corrupt input) turns into up to 5 sequential convert subprocess invocations on the same file inside one request, then the upload is created anyway at full original size — the exact state the feature was supposed to prevent — with no error surfaced to the user.

[BUG] The loop caps at 5 attempts of only 80% per pass (0.8^5 ≈ 0.33), so any image more than ~3.05x max_image_size_kb exits the loop still above the limit and is uploaded at that oversize size. With max_image_size_kb at its default of 1024KB, a 4MB photo ends the loop at ~1.31MB — still over the limit — and is stored as an oversize upload; the acceptance criterion 'reduced to allowed size' silently does not hold for the most common case (phone photos several times the limit), and no warning or rejection is issued.

[BUG] The `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` gate keys off the filename extension, and for the API URL path `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`, so any image URL whose path has no recognizable image extension (e.g. `https://example.com/image?w=800` or extensionless CDN routes) skips downsizing entirely. Large images fetched by URL without an extension are stored at full size with the oversize check silently bypassed — the failure mode the feature exists to close, reopened for a whole class of URLs.

[ADVISORY] The new downsizing loop is non-trivial behavior-bearing logic (loop with failure modes, animation gating, size arithmetic) and no spec or test file is added anywhere in this diff. Any regression in the loop — corrupted output, oversize passthrough, wrong settings guard — ships silently; nothing verifies the 5-attempt cap, the 0-size guard, or that non-images are skipped.

[ADVISORY] Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick subprocess invocations now run inside the uploads request/response cycle for every oversize image, where previously the controller only wrote the tempfile and inserted a row. Each large-image upload blocks a worker for the duration of multiple convert runs; a user uploading several multi-MB photos serializes worker capacity, and concurrent uploads can exhaust the web process pool — a hot-path regression with no queueing, timeout, or escape hatch.

[ADVISORY] Iterative 80% re-encoding means an image can pass through up to 5 generations of lossy re-encode (JPEG especially), when a single resize computed from the target size would reach the same result with one generation. Users' large images come back visibly degraded relative to a one-shot resize of the same final dimensions; the artifact-heavy output is what gets permanently stored and served.

[ADVISORY] The public class-method signature of `OptimizedImage.downsize` changes from `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` to `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` and the `OptimizedImage.dimensions` helper is deleted outright, with no deprecation shim. Out-of-tree plugins and themes calling the old 5-arg form hit `ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments)` at runtime after upgrade, and callers of the removed `dimensions` method hit NoMethodError — both with no warning at boot; the controller call in this diff works only because it was rewritten in the same commit.

[BUG] The client-side upload size check is hardcoded to `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;`, discarding the per-type `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup that previously governed every upload type (attachments, avatars, images). Site admins lose all configurability of upload limits from the browser: a site with max_attachment_size_kb=1024 now silently accepts 10MB attachments client-side, and a site with a 20MB image limit still rejects files over 10MB; the bootbox alert also reports a fixed '10240 KB' that bears no relation to any configured setting. This hardcoding is unrelated work smuggled into a feature about downsizing, and it is not reversible without a code deploy.

[BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes `max_image_size_kb` to `10 * 1024`, discarding `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. When the web server rejects an oversized upload with 413, the user is told the limit is '10240 KB' regardless of the site's actual configured max_image_size_kb, so the error message lies about the limit the server enforced; an admin who lowered max_image_size_kb to 512KB sees a message claiming 10MB.

[BUG] The API URL-download path hardcodes the download cap to `10.megabytes`, discarding `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. For API-driven URL uploads, the cap is silently raised for every site configured below 10MB: a site with max_image_size_kb=1024 now downloads and buffers up to 10MB of a remote URL (memory/disk cost per request, and the file is fetched even though it can never be accepted if it is a non-image attachment whose type limit is lower). Untraceable to the stated downsizing feature.

[BUG] The feature contradicts itself: the server-side downsizer accepts any image up to 10MB, but the concurrent client-side hardcode in utilities.js blocks browser uploads above 10MB, so 'automatically downsize large images' is never exercised for files larger than 10MB. A user with a 15MB photo — precisely the case the feature title names — is rejected client-side with 'file too large (10240 KB)' and the downsizing code never runs; symmetrically, an admin who raises max_image_size_kb above 10MB finds the setting unreachable from browser uploads. The two halves of this diff implement mutually exclusive policies for the same file range.

[ADVISORY] The downsizing loop never enforces its own invariant: it ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (false on convert failure) and exits after 5 iterations regardless of resulting size, so an image above max_image_size_kb can still reach Upload.create_for. Two concrete paths store an oversized upload: (1) ImageMagick fails (corrupt/unsupported image, disk full) and convert_with returns false, leaving the original oversized tempfile in place which is then uploaded as-is; (2) a file whose size needs more than 5 successive 80% reductions (0.8^5 ≈ 33% of original — e.g. a 6MB image on a site with a 512KB limit is still ~2MB after 5 passes) is uploaded oversized. The oversized file then fails downstream or bloats storage, silently — nothing logs or notifies.

[ADVISORY] The public `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature changes from `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` to `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` and the `dimensions` helper is removed, but the diff reshapes this shared model API to fit a single new caller that passes the non-obvious string "80%". Any caller (in-tree or plugin) still using the old four-argument form now has its width value interpreted as the dimensions string and its height argument lands in opts, producing a malformed ImageMagick instruction or an ArgumentError; and the new sole caller depends on the undocumented fact that downsize_instructions interpolates an ImageMagick geometry, so "80%" happens to work but nothing in the API communicates that a percentage is acceptable where WxH dimensions used to be required.

[BUG] The client-side size pre-check hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024`, discarding the per-type site setting `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` that previously drove it, so the browser now enforces a limit that is disconnected from the server's configured limit and from the new server-side downsizing feature. If an admin lowers max_attachment_size_kb to e.g. 1024, clients happily accept multi-MB attachments and only fail at the server; if the admin raises max_image_size_kb above 10MB (or relies on this PR's downsizing to accept images over the limit), the client refuses files the server would accept and shrink — the client check directly contradicts the feature this PR adds. Users are also shown a wrong limit (10240 KB) in the file_too_large message.

[BUG] The 413 handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, so the error message shown to the user asserts a limit that does not match the server's actual configured limit. Whenever max_image_size_kb is set to anything other than 10240 KB, a user whose upload is rejected by the web server is told the wrong maximum size and cannot correct the upload intelligently; the message also can't reflect per-type settings for non-image uploads hitting 413.

[BUG] The API URL-download path hardcodes the download cap at `10.megabytes`, replacing `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, so the two server-side upload paths now enforce different limits and contradict each other. With max_image_size_kb set above 10240 (e.g. 20480), a 15MB image POSTed as a file is accepted and downsized by the new block at lines 63-71, but the same image fetched via URL raises inside FileHelper.download, is swallowed by `rescue nil`, and the upload silently fails — an admin raising the setting to permit larger images gets no effect on the API URL path and no error surfaced to the API caller.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores the boolean return of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (convert_with returns false on non-zero exit and pipes output to /dev/null), so a permanently failing conversion is retried a fixed 5 times and the oversized file proceeds to Upload.create_for anyway. A corrupt or unreadable file with an image extension (or a host missing ImageMagick) causes 5 full ImageMagick invocations per upload request that all fail identically, with zero diagnostics (stderr discarded), and the user then gets only the generic oversized-file error downstream; every future caller of this pattern inherits the same silent-failure behavior.

[ADVISORY] Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions of files up to ~10MB are executed inline in the HTTP request thread, with no background job, timeout, or concurrency guard. Each convert on a large image takes seconds and significant CPU/memory, so a burst of large-image uploads serializes and stalls request workers (a scalability cliff on a hot path); this is a deliberate architecture choice that should at minimum be flagged — the existing optimized-image generation in Discourse runs out of request scope, and this inverts that ownership.

[ADVISORY] The call passes `tempfile.path` as `from`, and OptimizedImage's animated dispatch (`from =~ /\.GIF$/i` in optimize, model line 151) keys on that path, but Rack multipart tempfiles have no file extension, so the `_animated` instruction path is unreachable for uploads from this call site. Animated GIFs over the size limit are downsized through the static downsize_instructions path — the branch that exists precisely to handle multi-frame GIFs (allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is passed but can never take effect here) — so the animation handling the setting promises is silently skipped for exactly the files it is meant to protect.

[ADVISORY] The same 10MB quantity is now hand-written as three independent literals — `10 * 1024` (utilities.js:182), `10 * 1024` (utilities.js:246), `10.megabytes` (uploads_controller.rb:55) — with no single source of truth and only comments expressing the unit. The next editor who adjusts the cap will change one copy and not the others, silently desynchronizing the client pre-check, the 413 message, and the server download cap (the 86400-vs-84600 divergence class); all three should derive from one named constant or the site setting the code previously used.

[ADVISORY] The new non-trivial controller logic — the `max_image_size_kb > 0` gate, the FileHelper.is_image? extension gate, the 5-attempt cap, and the in-place tempfile mutation — ships with no test in this diff. A regression in any of these gates (e.g. the setting check inverted, or the loop condition comparing bytes against kilobytes) would silently break or skip downsizing for all uploads, and nothing in CI would catch it; the loop's interaction with SiteSetting values 0 and 1 in particular is unexercised.

[BUG] The client-side upload size check was silently changed from reading the admin-configured SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] to a hardcoded 10 * 1024, discarding the per-type site settings without any recorded acceptance of that objective change. Admins who configured max_image_size_kb (or per-type limits like max_avatar_size_kb) to anything other than 10MB get a client that enforces and displays a limit their admin panel no longer controls; the 'file_too_large' alert reports '10240 KB' regardless of the actual configured limit, so the user-facing error contradicts site configuration.

[BUG] The 413 error handler was silently changed from Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10 * 1024, replacing the setting-driven message with a fixed one. When the web server rejects an upload with 413 (its limit is configured in nginx, not here), the user is told the limit is 10MB even when the actual server limit or the admin's max_image_size_kb differs, so the error message is wrong for every site not using exactly 10MB.

[BUG] The API URL-download path was silently changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap, breaking the previously accepted behavior that admins control this limit via settings. API-driven URL imports of images larger than 10MB now fail with a 500 (FileHelper.download raises past the cap, `rescue nil` yields a nil tempfile, and Upload.create_for then calls .size on nil) even on sites where the admin deliberately raised max_image_size_kb for exactly this path; the same setting is still honored three lines later as the downsize target, so the diff mixes hardcoded and setting-driven limits on one request path.

[BUG] A second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is added while the first `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is left in place, so the later definition silently overrides the earlier one and the pre-existing 5-argument contract is replaced without preserving it. Any existing caller still using the old contract (from, to, max_width, max_height) crashes at runtime — 5 positional args raise ArgumentError ('wrong number of arguments (5 for 4)') and a 4-arg call binds the height Integer as opts, raising TypeError on opts[:allow_animation] — and the first definition at lines 146-148 becomes dead code that misleads readers into thinking both signatures work.

[BUG] The downsize loop gives up after 5 attempts of "80%" without verifying the resulting size, and OptimizedImage#convert_with discards the ImageMagick exit status, so the stated intent in the added comment — 'automatically reduced to allowed size' — is silently weakened to 'attempted at most 5 times'. A file that stays above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after 5 passes (each pass leaves ~64% of the pixels: 0.64^5 ≈ 10.7%, so a 50MB upload against a 4MB limit still lands at ~5MB) is uploaded oversized anyway, and if a convert invocation fails (binary missing, corrupt image) the untouched original is uploaded with no error surfaced to the user — the feature's acceptance criterion is not met on exactly the large-file cases it exists for.

[ADVISORY] optimize's public signature was changed from (operation, from, to, width, height, opts) to (operation, from, to, dimensions, opts) while the parameters are still named and used elsewhere as a 'WxH' string, a silent public-surface change for out-of-tree callers. Plugin or external code calling optimize directly with separate width/height now gets ArgumentError on 6 args, or binds the height Integer as opts and raises TypeError on opts[:allow_animation], with no deprecation path — the next person extending this API also has to reconcile that downsize now receives '80%' through a parameter named `dimensions` that every other caller supplies as 'WxH'.

[BUG] The new downsize path invokes ImageMagick (OptimizedImage.downsize -> convert_with backtick execution) on any upload whose filename merely has an image extension, before any content/magic-byte validation by UploadValidator runs in Upload.create_for. A user uploads arbitrary bytes named e.g. 'payload.png' larger than max_image_size_kb: previously such a file failed upload validation without ImageMagick ever parsing it; now it is piped through `convert` (including ImageMagick's format delegates) up to 5 times pre-validation, exposing the ImageMagick parser/delegate attack surface to fully untrusted input.

[ADVISORY] The retry loop spawns up to 5 ImageMagick processes per upload even when every downsize attempt fails, because a failed convert leaves tempfile.size unchanged and the loop only decrements `attempt`. A logged-in user repeatedly uploading corrupt or non-image files with an image extension forces 5 shell-out `convert` invocations per request (ImageMagick parse + error) with no short-circuit on failure, an easy CPU/process-count amplification lever on the upload endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The API URL-download cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes`, discarding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb as the server-side fetch limit for user-supplied URLs. An admin who lowered max_image_size_kb (e.g. to 1MB) to bound server-side fetch resource usage on the API upload path silently gets a 10MB cap instead; the configuration value stops controlling this sink without any operator-visible signal.

[BUG] The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value (false on convert failure via convert_with) and never re-validates the final size after the loop, so an upload that is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb is created and returned as success. When ImageMagick fails (not installed, corrupt image, exit status != 0) the unchanged oversized file is retried 5 times against the same failing command, then Upload.create_for proceeds; when conversions succeed but 5 iterations of 80% (≈33% of original) are insufficient for the file, the upload also completes. In both cases the API returns a successful upload response while the stored upload violates max_image_size_kb — the site limit is silently dropped with no error or log.

[BUG] The client-side pre-upload size check now hardcodes 10MB instead of reading the per-type site setting, so the browser enforces and reports a limit the administrator did not configure. Admins who set max_image_size_kb (or a non-image type's size limit) to anything other than 10MB get client behavior that contradicts their setting: files the client rejects with 'file_too_large, max_size_kb 10240' may be acceptable server-side, and files just under 10MB but above max_image_size_kb are the only ones that can ever reach the new server-side downsize path — the hardcoded client ceiling arbitrarily caps the feature this PR introduces.

[BUG] The 413 error handler reports a hardcoded '10 MB' as max_size_kb regardless of the server's actual configured limit, so the error message misdescribes the rejection. When nginx returns 413 because the configured limit is e.g. 4MB or 20MB, the user is told the maximum is 10240 KB; debugging 'why was my 6MB upload rejected when it says 10MB is allowed' misdirects both users and admins, and the message cannot be corrected without a code change.

[BUG] Hardcoding the API URL download cap at 10.megabytes regresses URL uploads of images between 10MB and a larger configured max_image_size_kb, and the swallowed download failure (rescue nil) then crashes at tempfile.size with a 500 instead of a 4xx. With max_image_size_kb set above 10MB, an API request uploading a 15MB image URL previously downloaded and processed fine; now FileHelper.download aborts at 10MB, the exception is swallowed by `rescue nil`, the downsize block is skipped via the nil guard, and `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, nil, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` raises NoMethodError on nil — the client gets a raw 500 for what is a too-large-upload condition.

[BUG] The animated-GIF branch in OptimizedImage.optimize keys on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` is tempfile.path (a Rack multipart Tempfile named like /tmp/RackMultipart… or the FileHelper prefix) which has no .GIF extension, so the _animated downsize instructions are never selected. Animated GIFs above max_image_size_kb are downsized with the non-animated instructions (no -coalesce), silently stripping or corrupting the animation while the upload still succeeds — the user's animated GIF becomes broken with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions of a file up to 10MB now run inline on the upload request thread with no timeout. A user uploading a large image that stays above the threshold blocks a web worker for the duration of 5 sequential convert invocations (each potentially seconds for a 10MB image); concurrent uploads of this kind can exhaust the worker pool and stall unrelated requests — this work has no async/queue path and no per-request timeout.

[ADVISORY] The 10MB limit is now hand-maintained as three independent literals (utilities.js line 182, utilities.js line 246, uploads_controller.rb line 55) instead of a single source of truth in SiteSetting. The next change to the cap must find and update three literals in two languages; missing one produces client/server limit divergence and wrong error messages, exactly the drift this diff already creates relative to max_image_size_kb which the same controller still reads two hunks below.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with from == to, making ImageMagick convert read and write the same file in place. convert reading and writing the same path is not a supported pattern; if the conversion fails partway through writing, the original tempfile contents are destroyed, and the corrupted/partial file is then passed to Upload.create_for and stored as a successful upload — corrupting the artifact precisely on the failure path.

This creates inconsistent server-side behavior when the setting is increased above 10MB: larger images could succeed via direct file upload (and be downsized) but fail via URL download due to the hard cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop ignores the boolean return of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (convert_with returns false on non-zero exit and pipes output to /dev/null), so a permanently failing conversion is retried a fixed 5 times and the oversized file proceeds to Upload.create_for anyway. A corrupt or unreadable file with an image extension (or a host missing ImageMagick) causes 5 full ImageMagick invocations per upload request that all fail identically, with zero diagnostics (stderr discarded), and the user then gets only the generic oversized-file error downstream; every future caller of this pattern inherits the same silent-failure behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop retries `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times purely based on `tempfile.size`, ignoring the method’s failure signal. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on non-zero exit (and otherwise returns `nil`), so a permanently failing ImageMagick invocation (corrupt/unreadable file, missing tools) will be retried 5 times with no diagnostics (`&> /dev/null`), and then the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` even if the file is still oversized. This is a real robustness/performance/correctness issue introduced by the new loop logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions of files up to ~10MB are executed inline in the HTTP request thread, with no background job, timeout, or concurrency guard. Each convert on a large image takes seconds and significant CPU/memory, so a burst of large-image uploads serializes and stalls request workers (a scalability cliff on a hot path); this is a deliberate architecture choice that should at minimum be flagged — the existing optimized-image generation in Discourse runs out of request scope, and this inverts that ownership.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds inline image downsizing in `UploadsController#create_upload`: a `while` loop (up to 5 iterations) calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` on the request path whenever an uploaded image exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (`uploads_controller.rb` new block). `OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize` ultimately runs ImageMagick via backticks in `convert_with`, which is synchronous and has no timeout/concurrency guard shown here. This is a concrete scalability/architecture concern introduced by the change rather than a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The call passes `tempfile.path` as `from`, and OptimizedImage's animated dispatch (`from =~ /\.GIF$/i` in optimize, model line 151) keys on that path, but Rack multipart tempfiles have no file extension, so the `_animated` instruction path is unreachable for uploads from this call site. Animated GIFs over the size limit are downsized through the static downsize_instructions path — the branch that exists precisely to handle multi-frame GIFs (allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is passed but can never take effect here) — so the animation handling the setting promises is silently skipped for exactly the files it is meant to protect.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true *and* `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Since `from` here is a tempfile filesystem path (not the original `filename`), it will typically not end in `.gif`, so `_animated` instructions won’t be used even when `allow_animation` is passed. This means oversized animated GIF uploads from this code path can be processed via the non-animated instructions, silently skipping the intended multi-frame handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same 10MB quantity is now hand-written as three independent literals — `10 * 1024` (utilities.js:182), `10 * 1024` (utilities.js:246), `10.megabytes` (uploads_controller.rb:55) — with no single source of truth and only comments expressing the unit. The next editor who adjusts the cap will change one copy and not the others, silently desynchronizing the client pre-check, the 413 message, and the server download cap (the 86400-vs-84600 divergence class); all three should derive from one named constant or the site setting the code previously used.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces prior uses of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` and `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with hard-coded 10MB caps in three places: `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in `utilities.js` (file size pre-check and 413 alert) and `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` in `uploads_controller.rb`. This creates duplicated literals without a shared constant or setting, so future changes can easily desynchronize the client pre-check, error messaging, and server-side download limit. It’s a concrete maintainability/consistency issue introduced by this diff, not an immediate functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new non-trivial controller logic — the `max_image_size_kb > 0` gate, the FileHelper.is_image? extension gate, the 5-attempt cap, and the in-place tempfile mutation — ships with no test in this diff. A regression in any of these gates (e.g. the setting check inverted, or the loop condition comparing bytes against kilobytes) would silently break or skip downsizing for all uploads, and nothing in CI would catch it; the loop's interaction with SiteSetting values 0 and 1 in particular is unexercised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new non-trivial behavior in `UploadsController#create_upload`: a conditional downsizing block gated by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0`, `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, a `while` loop comparing `tempfile.size` to `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, a hard cap of 5 attempts, and in-place mutation via `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`. No accompanying test changes/files are present in the diff, so regressions in these gates/units/loop behavior would not be covered by CI based on what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side upload size check was silently changed from reading the admin-configured SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] to a hardcoded 10 * 1024, discarding the per-type site settings without any recorded acceptance of that objective change. Admins who configured max_image_size_kb (or per-type limits like max_avatar_size_kb) to anything other than 10MB get a client that enforces and displays a limit their admin panel no longer controls; the 'file_too_large' alert reports '10240 KB' regardless of the actual configured limit, so the user-facing error contradicts site configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `utilities.js` replaces the client-side max size lookup (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`) with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) for both the initial check and the 413 error message. This removes per-type/admin-configured limits from the client and will display/enforce 10240KB regardless of actual configured settings, creating a clear client/server/config mismatch introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 413 error handler was silently changed from Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10 * 1024, replacing the setting-driven message with a fixed one. When the web server rejects an upload with 413 (its limit is configured in nginx, not here), the user is told the limit is 10MB even when the actual server limit or the admin's max_image_size_kb differs, so the error message is wrong for every site not using exactly 10MB.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the 413 error handler in `utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). That means the translated error message will always report 10MB regardless of the site’s configured `max_image_size_kb` (and regardless of any upstream web server limit that triggered the 413). This is a verifiable behavioral change in the diff and can produce incorrect/misleading user-facing output on sites not using a 10MB limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The API URL-download path was silently changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap, breaking the previously accepted behavior that admins control this limit via settings. API-driven URL imports of images larger than 10MB now fail with a 500 (FileHelper.download raises past the cap, `rescue nil` yields a nil tempfile, and Upload.create_for then calls .size on nil) even on sites where the admin deliberately raised max_image_size_kb for exactly this path; the same setting is still honored three lines later as the downsize target, so the diff mixes hardcoded and setting-driven limits on one request path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes the API URL-download size limit from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) rescue nil`). That breaks the previously setting-controlled behavior for API imports. Also, because the download is `rescue nil`, an oversize/failed download can yield `tempfile = nil`, and the method later unconditionally calls `tempfile.size` in `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)`, which would raise `NoMethodError` and 500. The same request path then uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` for the downsize loop, mixing hardcoded and setting-driven limits as the finding notes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is added while the first `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is left in place, so the later definition silently overrides the earlier one and the pre-existing 5-argument contract is replaced without preserving it. Any existing caller still using the old contract (from, to, max_width, max_height) crashes at runtime — 5 positional args raise ArgumentError ('wrong number of arguments (5 for 4)') and a 4-arg call binds the height Integer as opts, raising TypeError on opts[:allow_animation] — and the first definition at lines 146-148 becomes dead code that misleads readers into thinking both signatures work.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, the diff leaves the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` in place and then adds a later `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later method definition overrides the earlier one, so the 5-argument signature becomes dead code and any existing callers passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` will now raise `ArgumentError` (wrong number of arguments) at runtime. This defect is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop gives up after 5 attempts of "80%" without verifying the resulting size, and OptimizedImage#convert_with discards the ImageMagick exit status, so the stated intent in the added comment — 'automatically reduced to allowed size' — is silently weakened to 'attempted at most 5 times'. A file that stays above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after 5 passes (each pass leaves ~64% of the pixels: 0.64^5 ≈ 10.7%, so a 50MB upload against a 4MB limit still lands at ~5MB) is uploaded oversized anyway, and if a convert invocation fails (binary missing, corrupt image) the untouched original is uploaded with no error surfaced to the user — the feature's acceptance criterion is not met on exactly the large-file cases it exists for.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new “auto reduce” block loops at most 5 times (while `attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) and then unconditionally proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the (possibly still-oversized) `tempfile.size`; there is no post-loop check to reject/raise if the file remains above `max_image_size_kb`, so the comment’s promise (“automatically reduced to allowed size”) is not guaranteed by this diff. Additionally, OptimizedImage.convert_with returns `false` on nonzero exit status, but callers (the loop) ignore the return value, so a failed ImageMagick run can leave the original file intact and still uploaded with no user-visible error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] optimize's public signature was changed from (operation, from, to, width, height, opts) to (operation, from, to, dimensions, opts) while the parameters are still named and used elsewhere as a 'WxH' string, a silent public-surface change for out-of-tree callers. Plugin or external code calling optimize directly with separate width/height now gets ArgumentError on 6 args, or binds the height Integer as opts and raises TypeError on opts[:allow_animation], with no deprecation path — the next person extending this API also has to reconcile that downsize now receives '80%' through a parameter named `dimensions` that every other caller supplies as 'WxH'.

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize`’s arity is changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={})` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, and `downsize` is accidentally defined twice: first as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then redefined as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, which in Ruby overwrites the prior definition. As a result, any existing callers (including plugins/out-of-tree) passing separate width/height (or calling `optimize` with 6 args) will now raise `ArgumentError` at runtime. This is a real breaking behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new downsize path invokes ImageMagick (OptimizedImage.downsize -> convert_with backtick execution) on any upload whose filename merely has an image extension, before any content/magic-byte validation by UploadValidator runs in Upload.create_for. A user uploads arbitrary bytes named e.g. 'payload.png' larger than max_image_size_kb: previously such a file failed upload validation without ImageMagick ever parsing it; now it is piped through `convert` (including ImageMagick's format delegates) up to 5 times pre-validation, exposing the ImageMagick parser/delegate attack surface to fully untrusted input.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new pre-processing block runs before `Upload.create_for(...)` and thus before any validation that `Upload.create_for` might perform. The condition `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is based on the provided `filename` (derived from URL basename or the uploaded file name), and if it returns true and the tempfile is oversized, it calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times on the raw tempfile. `OptimizedImage.downsize` leads to `convert_with`, which executes ImageMagick via backticks on that untrusted content. This diff therefore introduces an earlier ImageMagick parse/convert step on potentially unvalidated input, expanding the attack surface compared to the prior code path that went straight to `Upload.create_for`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry loop spawns up to 5 ImageMagick processes per upload even when every downsize attempt fails, because a failed convert leaves tempfile.size unchanged and the loop only decrements `attempt`. A logged-in user repeatedly uploading corrupt or non-image files with an image extension forces 5 shell-out `convert` invocations per request (ImageMagick parse + error) with no short-circuit on failure, an easy CPU/process-count amplification lever on the upload endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new retry loop (`attempt = 5; while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...; OptimizedImage.downsize(...); attempt -= 1`) never checks whether `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`convert_with` succeeded. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` on nonzero exit status, but that return value is ignored, so a failing ImageMagick invocation will leave `tempfile.size` unchanged and the loop will still run up to 5 times. This enables up to 5 shell-outs per request for files that pass `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` but cannot be processed (e.g., corrupt content with an image-like filename).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The API URL-download cap is hardcoded to `10.megabytes`, discarding SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb as the server-side fetch limit for user-supplied URLs. An admin who lowered max_image_size_kb (e.g. to 1MB) to bound server-side fetch resource usage on the API upload path silently gets a 10MB cap instead; the configuration value stops controlling this sink without any operator-visible signal.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL-download path changes from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, which demonstrably ignores the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` for server-side URL fetching. This means an admin-set lower cap no longer constrains that download resource usage, with no indication in the shown diff that the setting is respected elsewhere for this operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value (false on convert failure via convert_with) and never re-validates the final size after the loop, so an upload that is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb is created and returned as success. When ImageMagick fails (not installed, corrupt image, exit status != 0) the unchanged oversized file is retried 5 times against the same failing command, then Upload.create_for proceeds; when conversions succeed but 5 iterations of 80% (≈33% of original) are insufficient for the file, the upload also completes. In both cases the API returns a successful upload response while the stored upload violates max_image_size_kb — the site limit is silently dropped with no error or log.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new loop attempts to downsize images while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but it never checks whether `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` succeeded (it can return `false` when `convert_with` fails) and it does not enforce/validate that the file is actually <= the configured limit after the loop exits. After 5 attempts it proceeds unconditionally to `Upload.create_for(...)` with whatever size remains, so the new “automatically reduced to allowed size” behavior is not guaranteed by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side pre-upload size check now hardcodes 10MB instead of reading the per-type site setting, so the browser enforces and reports a limit the administrator did not configure. Admins who set max_image_size_kb (or a non-image type's size limit) to anything other than 10MB get client behavior that contradicts their setting: files the client rejects with 'file_too_large, max_size_kb 10240' may be acceptable server-side, and files just under 10MB but above max_image_size_kb are the only ones that can ever reach the new server-side downsize path — the hardcoded client ceiling arbitrarily caps the feature this PR introduces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes the client-side max upload size to `10 * 1024` KB (10MB) in two places in `utilities.js`, replacing reads from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. This makes the browser-side enforcement/reporting diverge from admin-configured per-type limits (e.g., higher limits will be incorrectly blocked at 10MB, and non-image types no longer respect their settings). This is directly shown by the replaced lines in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 413 error handler reports a hardcoded '10 MB' as max_size_kb regardless of the server's actual configured limit, so the error message misdescribes the rejection. When nginx returns 413 because the configured limit is e.g. 4MB or 20MB, the user is told the maximum is 10240 KB; debugging 'why was my 6MB upload rejected when it says 10MB is allowed' misdirects both users and admins, and the message cannot be corrected without a code change.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js`, the 413 handler now hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` (10MB) instead of using `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` (see the change in the `case 413:` block). That makes the displayed `post.errors.file_too_large` message potentially incorrect whenever the actual reject limit differs (e.g., reverse proxy/nginx `client_max_body_size`), matching the finding’s complaint about misdescribing the rejection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Hardcoding the API URL download cap at 10.megabytes regresses URL uploads of images between 10MB and a larger configured max_image_size_kb, and the swallowed download failure (rescue nil) then crashes at tempfile.size with a 500 instead of a 4xx. With max_image_size_kb set above 10MB, an API request uploading a 15MB image URL previously downloaded and processed fine; now FileHelper.download aborts at 10MB, the exception is swallowed by `rescue nil`, the downsize block is skipped via the nil guard, and `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, nil, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` raises NoMethodError on nil — the client gets a raw 500 for what is a too-large-upload condition.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL download limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, which can regress behavior when `max_image_size_kb` is configured > 10MB (URL downloads >10MB will now fail earlier than the configured limit). Additionally, the download is still wrapped in `rescue nil`, and the code later unconditionally calls `tempfile.size` in `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` even if `tempfile` is nil (the new downsize block guards `tempfile`, but the `Upload.create_for` call does not), so a failed download can lead to a 500 via `NoMethodError` on `nil.size`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The animated-GIF branch in OptimizedImage.optimize keys on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` is tempfile.path (a Rack multipart Tempfile named like /tmp/RackMultipart… or the FileHelper prefix) which has no .GIF extension, so the _animated downsize instructions are never selected. Animated GIFs above max_image_size_kb are downsized with the non-animated instructions (no -coalesce), silently stripping or corrupting the animation while the upload still succeeds — the user's animated GIF becomes broken with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The new upload-resizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` in `uploads_controller.rb`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is selected only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is a tempfile path (e.g., Rack multipart temp paths or `FileHelper.download` temp paths) that typically has no `.gif` extension. So even for an actual animated GIF, `_animated` instructions will not be chosen, and the non-animated downsize path will be used. This is a correctness bug introduced/exposed by adding downsizing on tempfiles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions of a file up to 10MB now run inline on the upload request thread with no timeout. A user uploading a large image that stays above the threshold blocks a web worker for the duration of 5 sequential convert invocations (each potentially seconds for a 10MB image); concurrent uploads of this kind can exhaust the worker pool and stall unrelated requests — this work has no async/queue path and no per-request timeout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an inline loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can run up to 5 `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` calls synchronously on the request thread while the tempfile remains larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...`). `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes ImageMagick via backticks with no timeout or async/queue mechanism shown, so large/slow conversions can block a web worker for multiple sequential invocations. This is a concrete perf/worker-exhaustion risk introduced by the change, though not a direct correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 10MB limit is now hand-maintained as three independent literals (utilities.js line 182, utilities.js line 246, uploads_controller.rb line 55) instead of a single source of truth in SiteSetting. The next change to the cap must find and update three literals in two languages; missing one produces client/server limit divergence and wrong error messages, exactly the drift this diff already creates relative to max_image_size_kb which the same controller still reads two hunks below.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces SiteSetting-based max size checks with hard-coded 10MB literals in two JS locations (`var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;`) and in the controller URL-download limit (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). Meanwhile, the same controller still references `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` a few lines later for the new downsize loop, meaning upload behavior/error messaging can diverge from the configured SiteSetting. This is a concrete client/server/config drift introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with from == to, making ImageMagick convert read and write the same file in place. convert reading and writing the same path is not a supported pattern; if the conversion fails partway through writing, the original tempfile contents are destroyed, and the corrupted/partial file is then passed to Upload.create_for and stored as a successful upload — corrupting the artifact precisely on the failure path.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e. `from == to`. In `OptimizedImage`, `downsize` delegates to `optimize`, which builds ImageMagick instructions and executes them via backticks in `convert_with(instructions, to)`, writing output to `to` (the same path as the input). The diff also shows the return value from `convert_with` (false on nonzero exit) is ignored by `optimize` and by the controller loop, so a failed/partial in-place write could leave a corrupted tempfile that is still passed to `Upload.create_for` as if successful.
